budgetLedger.description: Budget ledger for the run, owned by the root coordinator. Dollars primary. Every spawn is a reservation, refused when it would exceed the remaining amount. Unused reservations are refunded. Reserve held back for verification and the dead-end report is at least 15 percent. Where the platform cannot block further calls at the limit, the limit is labelled advisory in the manifest, and is never presented as a hard control.

checkCommand.description: The single VERIFY command for this unit.

whyCheap.description: Why this unit is cheap: small, low risk, reversible, checkable with one command.

trigger.description: Which registry trigger fired. Must match the trigger in router/router-registry.md for this skill.

why.description: Why this skill, for this case.

risk.description: Tool risk rating, by read vs write, reversibility, permissions, and cost. High-risk tools pause for a check or go to a human.

targets.description: Targets this tool may touch for this run, for example path prefixes, repos, or URL hosts.

dependsOn.description: Names of units this unit needs. No entries means parallel. Two or more entries makes this unit a join.

description: One file that states what a human authorized a Handover run to do. Matches Handover v7, skills/handover/SKILL.md, Step 2. The manifest is what was authorized, not the prose package alone. Generated instructions are untrusted until validated against the manifest. The budget ledger, tool risk ratings, failure threshold N, cheap-unit collapse declarations, and Discovery router call log are v7 additions: the skill text already required them, the v4 schema did not carry them. This schema states the shape only. It does not enforce anything at run time. Until the Stage 2 harness ships, enforcement rests on the coordinator, the verifier, and the judge, plus scripts/check-handover.sh as a static check.

cheapUnits.description: Cheap-unit collapse declarations, written before the run. Each names the unit, why it is cheap, and its single check command. Empty when no unit is cheap. Never call a unit cheap after the fact to skip a check.

date.description: Date the manifest was written, YYYY-MM-DD.

failureThresholdN.description: When the same tool fails N times in a row, stop retrying it and escalate to a human. N is set here, for the run.

kit.description: Field kit named in Stage 1, Case A (existing proven kit) or Case B (kit to be generated). There is no third case.

manifestVersion.description: Version id of this manifest, for example stage2-router-wire-2026-11-15-01.

notes.description: Notes on the rendering of this manifest, for example where a field was added when a prose original was rendered as JSON.

oneWayDoors.description: Outward actions authorized for this run, each listed exactly with action, destination, limit, and condition. Empty when none is authorized.

predicateVersion.description: Version id of the finish predicate this manifest runs under. A predicate amendment creates a new version and voids verdicts tied to the old one.

prohibitedActions.description: Actions this run must not do, in plain words.

routerCallLog.description: Discovery router call log. One entry per Discovery skill call, written before the call: what the coordinator saw, which trigger fired, and why this skill. A call without a line does not happen.

runId.description: Run id, usually the same as manifestVersion.

stage1Version.description: Version id of the approved Stage 1 package this manifest runs under.

tools.description: Tools and targets allowlist for the run. Each entry carries a risk rating: low, medium, or high, by read vs write, reversibility, permissions, and cost. Everything not listed is denied or routed to approval.

units.description: Per-unit list. Each unit has one output file or folder, one owner, one check. Passes starts false for every unit.

title: Handover Stage 2 execution manifest
